text.p: SME - The National Property Fund (NPF), the state privatisation agency, sold state property worth some 33.4 billion crowns in 1996. It has sold off more than 329 billion crowns worth of assets since 1990 when the Slovak privatisation process started. The privatisers owed the NPF more than six billion crowns as of the end of 1996.

- Five opposition parties sent a letter to U.S. President Bill Clinton asking him not to lose interest in Slovakia after the NATO summit in Madrid next week. They announced they were planning to enter next year's general elections as a common bloc.

NARODNA OBRODA - The five opposition parties, led by the Christian Democrats (KDH) and Democratic Union (DU), which formed a coalition bloc this week have yet to agree on its leader. The name of the new coalition chief will be known probably only after the summer.

- Minister of Education Eva Slavkovska said the controversial history book, "The History of Slovakia and the Slovaks", which was ordered to be withdrawn from schools after European Union criticism, would stay in school libraries for voluntary use.

- The police trade union (OZP) decided to cancel a demonstration, scheduled for Friday, to protest against poor financial conditions. It said it had cancelled the protest after Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar's public promise that their problems, including increasing their salaries, will be solved.

PRAVDA - The state railways, ZSR, posted a loss of 497 million crowns in 1996 and some two billion crowns in the first five months of this year due to many disadvantageous contracts it had concluded. The new management of the company said it planned to restructure the workforce of the railways.
